newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian wool, cotton seen making ground.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian wool, cotton seen making ground.

text.p: Wool prices are expected to rise over the medium-term but synthetics are expected to capture a greater share of the growing world fibre market, official forecasting agency the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) said.

In papers to be presented at its Outlook conference, ABARE forecast Australia's eastern market indicator price for wool would rise to an average of 650 cents a kg in 1997/98 from the average of 580 cents in the first half of 1996/97.
It forecast that prices would improve to bring the indicator to an average of 600 cents a kg in 1996/97 as a whole.
Lower prices in first first half of 1996/97 resulted from flat demand and increased availability of wool for sale, it said.
Slight rises in prices over the remainder of 1996/97 were expected to result from improvements in retail consumption and processing activity in Japan, China and the U.S.
Further price improvements in 1997/98 were expected to result from little change in world supply and a sustained steady improvement in retail demand, it said.

Forecast higher production from Australia, at 710,000 tonnes in 1997/98, up from 682,000 tonnes in 1996/97 and 697,000 tonnes the year before, was expected to be offset by lower sales from stocks, it said.
Looking further ahead, wool prices were projected to recover steadily to average 743 cents a kg in 1996/97 terms in year 2001/02, 24 percent above the forecast 1996/97 average, it said.
The major influence on price was expected to be reduced wool availability toward the end of the outlook period and growth in consumer income in developed and developing countries, it said.
But ABARE said also that synthetics and cotton dominate the world fibre market, accounting for 48.0 percent and 44.0 percent respectively. Wool accounts for only about four percent.
But Australia's 1997/98 lint production is forecast to dip to 557,000 tonnes from the record harvest 571,000 tonnes forecast for 1996/97.
The forecast 1996/97 production, steady with ABARE's previous forecast in December, is up from 429,000 tonnes in 1995/96.
After the 1997/98 dip, Australian production is forecast to rise to 683,000 tonnes in year 2001/02.
This would follow an increase in area harvested, to 420,000 hectares in year 2001/02 from 301,000 ha in 1995/96.
Area harvested in 1997/98 is forecast at 363,000 ha, down on the current year.

"Lower grain prices, bountiful irrigation water, good soil moisture levels and high returns for irrigated cotton relative to other crops are reflected in the record plantings of 388,000 ha in 1996/97," ABARE said.
